solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: (& 5dn.) "Opposing cut, one's put in spot" – one of Brenda's

indicators.note: something put in a place sits inside it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: bucking a trend is opposing it
ham is a cut of meat from a pig's leg
a spot is a place
one is A, the indefinite article; the apostrophe s is 'is'

explanation.surface: A satirical jibe about someone being opposed, cut down and put in their place, aimed at a royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, so 'one of Brenda's' means one of her residences.
explanation.definitionFit: The London residence of the British monarch was one of the late Queen's official homes.

clue.text: Like nothing on earth, Dave's butt, squeezed into fancy leather!

indicators.note: a butt is the tail end of something, so only the final letter of the name is kept
squeezed into means pushed inside, so one piece goes within the other
fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Dave

explanation.surface: David Cameron's backside squeezed into kinky leather is a sight like nothing on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave is Private Eye's David Cameron, but here only the last letter of his name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something delicate and heavenly, too light and otherworldly to seem of this world.

clue.text: Once deemed OK by lending banks quick to bring lawyer back in

definitions.text: Once deemed OK by lending banks

indicators.note: going back means reading the lawyer's title from right to left
to bring something in is to put it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: brisk means quick
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A dig at banks which once rushed to lend, and now hurry to bring in lawyers to get their money back.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sardonic description: subprime borrowers were happily lent to before the crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrower unlikely to repay is a poor credit prospect, yet before the financial crash banks lent to such people freely.

clue.text: No stranger to being on the road, Trump, at heart, scared witless

definitions.text: No stranger to being on the road

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept
witless means senseless and confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the middle letter of Trump
the letters of scared rearranged

explanation.surface: Donald Trump, a seasoned campaigner on the road, is nonetheless frightened out of his wits.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand vehicle has already covered plenty of miles, so it is well accustomed to travelling on highways.

clue.text: see 1dn.
see 26dn.
Jerk's hacked my second SIM, disseminating 'spirituality'

indicators.note: here second is the ordinary abbreviation s for a second of time, a single kept letter
disseminating means scattering widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
a hacker breaks into a phone, so the jerk gets inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
s is the abbreviation for second
a tic is an involuntary jerk; the apostrophe s is 'has'
the letters of SIM rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an idiot has hacked their second phone SIM card and is spreading spiritual messages.
explanation.walkthrough: The tic goes between MYS and ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysticism is the pursuit of union with the divine through contemplation, a form of spiritual belief and practice.

clue.text: Fliers making Apple mad?

blocks.note: an apple is an example of fruit
bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of airline travellers would drive the Apple technology company crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A makes Apple look like the tech company; it is just the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: These large tropical bats are winged mammals, so they are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Corporate excess: strong links with political party

indicators.note: to link with something is to join up with it, so the pieces are placed side by side

blocks.note: f is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A business-page tale of corporate waste and companies cosying up to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporate' here means bodily, from corpus, not to do with companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate can mean of the body, and soft surplus fat on the body is excess bulk.

clue.text: Bellow applied to one's back passage

indicators.note: back tells us the word for bellow is read backwards

blocks.note: one is A, the indefinite article
to bellow is to yell

explanation.surface: A rude suggestion of shouting directly at someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back passage' looks like one smutty phrase, but 'back' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane or walkway between buildings, a kind of thoroughfare.

clue.text: Burn head off joint

indicators.note: with its head off a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to rankle is to burn with lingering resentment

explanation.surface: An instruction that sounds like smoking a joint after burning its tip off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge between the foot and the leg, one of the body's articulations.

clue.text: Arse injected with copper – dear treatment as befits a VIP?

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the policeman's letters go into the other word

blocks.note: the rear is the backside
DC is a detective constable, a police officer
pet is an affectionate word like dear

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a backside injected with metal, with a sly question about whether celebrities get such treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the metal, but it is slang for a police officer. Redcar, the seaside town, appears on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Important guests are welcomed by rolling out a crimson rug, so the phrase means lavish ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: Oral massages producing desires

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: to knead muscles is to massage them; the silent K disappears when spoken

explanation.surface: A suggestive hint that oral sex and massages stir up desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs and desires are both things a person wants or requires, used here as plural nouns.

clue.text: Care to get screwed by writer's tart?

indicators.note: something screwed up is twisted out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of care rearranged
a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writing tool

explanation.surface: A lewd question about whether someone wants to sleep with a novelist's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the sexual slang of the surface, but here it is the adjective for sharp or sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic remarks are sharp and biting in tone, just as a tart reply is cutting.

clue.text: Dictator offers grand whorehouse, right for leader of Lords

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
putting one thing for another means swapping it in, so one letter replaces another

blocks.note: grand means big
a brothel is a whorehouse
R is the abbreviation for right
the first letter of Lords

explanation.surface: A tyrant lays on a lavish bordello, with someone righteous replacing the head of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: In BROTHEL the L is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is the all-seeing ruler in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, so the name stands for any authoritarian ruler.

clue.text: Journalist sap swallows Dave's introduction: "Not yet tried"

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is kept
whatever is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper
sap is the juice of a plant
the first letter of Dave

explanation.surface: A gullible hack swallows David Cameron's account and reports something as unproven.
explanation.walkthrough: Sap looks like a fool here, but it is the fluid in a plant. D goes inside JUICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under judicial consideration has not yet been decided by a court, so it cannot be discussed.

clue.text: (& 18dn.) Union hall lay in ruins, stuffing taken out of corrosive Lib Dem-Tory coalition?

indicators.note: something in ruins has collapsed into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
removing the stuffing leaves only the outside, so just the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of corrosive

explanation.surface: A union building wrecked and gutted becomes an image for the damaging Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government of 2010-15.
explanation.definitionFit: An unholy alliance is a pact between unlikely partners, and the question mark marks the Cameron-Clegg government as one example.

clue.text: Tentative shag, imbibing endless booze, which is not to everyone's taste

definitions.text: which is not to everyone's taste

indicators.note: a tentative attempt is hesitant and unsettled, so the letters are moved about
endless means the final letter is dropped
imbibing is drinking in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of shag rearranged
gin is a type of booze

explanation.surface: A hesitant sexual encounter fuelled by bottomless drinking, which not everyone would enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: Scotland's national dish of offal is famously divisive.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish pudding of sheep's offal, oatmeal and suet is loved by some diners and loathed by many.

clue.text: see 16ac.
Enters presidential race – after Trump's second interruption, leaves in helpless position

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the name
an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: a candidate stands for office
the second letter of Trump

explanation.surface: Someone announces a run for president and, after a Trump heckle, is left stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside STANDS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to abandon them somewhere with no way out, as a beached ship is marooned.

clue.text: see 22dn.
Have a bonk and spurt – most direct means of getting high?

definitions.text: most direct means of getting high

blocks.note: jump is slang for having sex; bonk is British slang for the same
a jet is a spurt of liquid

explanation.surface: A crude account of quick sex as the fastest route to a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting high' suggests drugs or sex, but it means gaining altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A Harrier-type warplane takes off vertically, so it rises straight up into the sky without a runway.

clue.text: (& 20dn.) Hunt opponents using dodgy journo's dirt about odious Conservative leaders

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable and suspect, so the letters are moved about
about means around, so these letters wrap the others
the leaders of words are their first letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letters of odious and Conservative

explanation.surface: Opponents of Jeremy Hunt use a shady reporter's smears about nasty Tory leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt was the Conservative Health Secretary whose 2016 contract dispute with hospital trainees led to strikes; 'Hunt' is not a fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital doctors below consultant level went on strike against Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt's new contract in 2016.

clue.text: Randy exploiter of viewers

blocks.note: surface reading: a lecherous TV executive who takes advantage of the audience
setter's reading: viewers are eyes, and a lustful person uses their own eyes to stare at others

explanation.walkthrough: Viewers sounds like a television audience, but it means eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leers lustfully at people is using their eyes for lecherous purposes.

clue.text: Shit drug charge

blocks.note: C is slang for cocaine
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.definitionFit: Both words are vulgar slang nouns for excrement, and also for anything worthless.

clue.text: Balls retracted to resist TV personality, one in suit?

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the politician's first name is read backwards

blocks.note: Ed Balls is a former Labour politician turned TV personality
to fend off is to resist
Ant McPartlin is half of the British presenting duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A painful picture of testicles withdrawing in fear of a TV star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is the surname of Ed Balls, Labour minister and Strictly Come Dancing contestant, not anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit has a person accused or sued, the party who answers the case in court.

clue.text: (& 6dn.) Scum Conservative's on edge – not much to see

blocks.note: scum is a thin film on the surface of a liquid
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A sneer at a Tory politician who is nervous and has little worth looking at.
explanation.definitionFit: A short excerpt of footage lasts only seconds, so it offers viewers only a brief glimpse.

clue.text: Fart around, recruiting last vestige of Nige's following

indicators.note: around suggests messing about, so the letters are moved into a new order
recruiting means taking someone in, so a letter goes inside
the last vestige of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Nige

explanation.surface: Some layabout fooling around ends up signing up the last of Nigel Farage's supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Nige is Nigel Farage, the Brexit-campaigning politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Following and after both describe something that comes later in time or sequence.

clue.text: Where you might find a monk with nothing on, source of pleasure between the legs

definitions.text: source of pleasure between the legs

blocks.clueFragment: Where you might find a monk
blocks.note: a monk lives in a small room called a cell
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A naked monk in a cell is cast in a distinctly unholy light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pleasure between the legs' is cheekily innocent: the large stringed instrument is held between a seated player's knees.

clue.text: Scandal on Twitter said to be greatly discounted

blocks.note: dirt is scandalous gossip
to twitter like a bird is to cheep

explanation.surface: Scandal spread on social media is said to make something worth very little.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitter suggests the social network, but it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold for next to nothing is very inexpensive, marked down far below normal price.
